paragraphs.text: Parallels: Pri Tzaddik, Shemot 5 — the same two prayers ("Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah and make our heart cleave" and "May He open our heart to His Torah… and place in our heart His love and fear"), with Torah as Jacob's "kol" that gives life to speech.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 60:8. "The conversation of the servants of the Patriarchs' households is finer than the Torah of their sons: the section of Eliezer runs two or three columns, and he tells it and repeats it" — Eliezer's story is told and retold at length, while key laws are learned only from hints. Rav Tzadok: the length shows that the parashah holds hidden secrets.

paragraphs.text: Siddur, Ahavah Rabbah (blessing before the morning Shema). "Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah, make our heart cleave to Your commandments, and unite our heart to love and to fear Your Name, and let us not be ashamed… for in Your great (mighty) and awesome holy Name we have trusted; let us rejoice and be glad in Your salvation; and may Your mercy, Lord our God, and Your abundant kindnesses never forsake us, forever, selah, and eternally" (Nusach Sefard). The rest of the maamar reads this blessing phrase by phrase.

"The heart and the eye are the two brokers of sin… The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If you give Me your heart and your eyes, I know that you are Mine." — that darkens the faces of creatures," etc.,

— all the blemish from the serpent,

h: A salvation that does not lapse

p: — "May they never forsake us, forever and ever":
— that the salvation be for all eternity,
— and not as it was at the giving of the Torah,
— when, as they heard the utterance "You shall have no…,"
— the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart,
— the evil inclination returned to its place,
, — (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on "Let him kiss me").
— Rather, that the salvation be eternal—
— And in the manner of the verse:
— you shall not be ashamed," etc.
— This accords with what was said:
— "'and the disgrace of His people He will remove'—
— this is the evil inclination," etc.;

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4. "Rabbi Nechemiah said: When Israel heard 'You shall have no [other gods],' the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart… immediately the evil inclination returned to its place" — the removal at Sinai was temporary; the hoped-for salvation is "forever, selah, and eternally." Printing fix: "ne'ekav" corrected to "ne'ekar" ("was uprooted").

p: — which corresponds to the holiness of Jacob our father,

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 129a (Idra Rabba): "And when it is revealed, the prayers of Israel are accepted. When is it revealed? ... He said to him: At the hour of the Minchah prayer of Shabbat. He said to him: What is the reason? He said to him: Because at that hour on weekdays judgment hangs below in Ze'ir Anpin, but on Shabbat the Forehead called Ratzon (Favor) is revealed; at that hour anger subsides, favor is found, and prayer is accepted, as it is written, 'And as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, in a time of favor' (Psalms 69:14). And the time of favor comes from the Ancient of Days, to reveal the Forehead; and therefore this verse was established to be said in the Minchah prayer on Shabbat." This is the passage Rav Tzadok means by "as it says earlier": the Idra itself ties the "time of favor" to Shabbat Minchah.
